title: GUARD — was: with zsh/complist loaded, a format style's %F/%K/%f/%k printed no colour, %F{nosuch} leaked its name, %F{bl} did not resolve to black, and every listing newline carried an unconditional CSI K

spec.completer:
#compdef fzc6000
_wanted alpha expl 'al' compadd -- a1 b2; _wanted beta expl 'be' compadd -- c1

observed.measured: 2026-10-30, debug build of main + this fix vs zsh 5.9.2 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0)
observed.notes: complist's compprintfmt (5.9.2 Src/Zle/complist.c:1164-1186) writes %F/%K/%f/%k through set_colour_attribute; match_named_colour (Src/prompt.c:1923-1927) advances past a failed name and matches by prefix; compprintnl (complist.c:1058) erases only through cleareol, which is gated on mlbeg >= 0 (complist.c:610).

observed_when_diverging.detail: 3 row(s) differ in SGR attributes only (with the colour arms already ported); before that, the %F{nosuch} rows differed in text: zsh '<al> x y z', zshrs '<al> x y nosuch}z'
observed_when_diverging.notes: raw stream at that point: zsh wrote \e[30m before 'w' (%F{bl}) and zshrs did not; zshrs wrote \e[K after the %3K{green row and after each listing row where zsh wrote nothing, painting the header row green. Without the colour arms, '%F{blue}<%d>%f' printed the header uncoloured (zsh: \e[34m ... \e[39m).
